checks.name: make-secrets
checks.summary: MEASURED FAILURE, and it is not caused by this change. `gitleaks git` reports 'leaks found: 4' after scanning 455 commits. All four findings are generic-api-key false positives on evidence prose of the shape 'evidence_key = <64 hex> This value is recor...', in these files and commits: .agents/v2/evidence/V2-058-runner.json and .agents/v2/evidence/V2-058-application.json at commit e1c46da03338c773e6531950e741c10d63aa5852, and two findings in .agents/v2/evidence/V2-045-candidate-aggregate.json at commit ae9a178a463d53c34544b8c43c768c5d25f126af. Measured with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`: NEITHER commit is an ancestor of this branch's HEAD. Measured with `git branch -a --contains`: e1c46da is contained only by v2-task/V2-058 and ae9a178 only by v2-task/V2-045 -- two other tasks' in-flight branches. docs/architecture/validation.md L187 records that `gitleaks git` scans every ref in the repository, and this worktree shares its object store with those branches, so the gate reads their commits too. Scoped re-measurements on this task's own content, both green: `gitleaks git --log-opts=HEAD` scanned 295 commits and reported 'no leaks found'; `gitleaks dir .` scanned the whole working tree and reported 'no leaks found'. This task therefore introduces no finding and cannot clear the four that exist: the offending files are under .agents/v2/evidence/ on branches this task must not touch, and .gitleaks.toml is outside allowed_paths. Recorded as a failure rather than as a pass, and escalated to the tech_lead.
